simple.meaning: בַּעַל בְּרִית (Baʻal Bᵉrîyth) is a Hebrew word meaning “Baal-Berith , a special deity of the Shechemites.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: בַּעַל בְּרִית (H1170) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Judges 8:33, with occurrences in Judges.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בַּעַל בְּרִית (H1170) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in בַּעַל בְּרִית (H1170) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: בַּעַל בְּרִית (Baʻal Bᵉrîyth) / H1170 is traced through Judges 8:33, Judges 9:4 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

occurrences.englishText: As soon as Gideon was dead, the children of Israel turned again and played the prostitute following the Baals, and made Baal Berith their god.
They gave him seventy pieces of silver out of the house of Baal Berith, with which Abimelech hired vain and reckless fellows who followed him.
